newsitem.title: LEBANON: First bank shares trade on Beirut Stock Exchange.
newsitem.headline: First bank shares trade on Beirut Stock Exchange.

text.p: Shares of Banque Libanaise Pour Le Commerce were traded on Monday on the Beirut Stock Exchange for the first time when 2,000 shares changed hands at $11.25.
The BLC is the first bank to trade on the Beirut Stock Exchange (BSE) under a recent law allowing banks to trade 30 percent of their shares.
Solidere shares rose on higher turnover on the BSE as A shares rose to $112.125 from Friday's $109.75 and B shares rose to $115 from $114.
Turnover in Solidere shares sharply rose to 34,374 shares from Friday's 7,722 and value was $3,865,072.5 from $833,397.
The BLC ranked 14th among Lebanon's 82 commercial banks in 1994 in the size of its customer deposits.
There was no trade in the shares of the four other listed companies: Ciments Libanais, Ciments Blancs, Eternit and Uniceramic.
The LISPI stock index rose 0.43 percent to 81.78 and the BLOM stock index also rose 0.19 percent to 948.11.
